clue.text: Cheap beer makes my bum look big in this

definitions.text: makes my bum look big in this

parts.note: a farthing was the old quarter-penny coin, a byword for something of almost no value
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone worries that a cheap pint will add inches to their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was the smallest old British coin, worth a quarter of a penny, so it stands for anything cheap. The surface reads 'Cheap beer' as one idea, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This hooped Tudor petticoat held skirts out wide at the hips, padding out the wearer's rear.

clue.text: Tree's fewer leaves, perhaps, losing top

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word is dropped in this down clue

parts.note: a tree that is balder has fewer leaves left on it, the 'perhaps' marking an example

explanation.surface: A tree is losing its leaves at the crown in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: BALDER (having less hair, or here fewer leaves) loses its first letter B; the 's after 'Tree' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Quiz polished off with a will?

parts.note: a quiz is a test of knowledge
to polish off food is to eat it all, past tense ate

explanation.surface: Someone finished an exam paper with real determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' looks like 'enthusiastically', but it means having left a legal will; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has made a valid legal will before death.

clue.text: Published 'eye' we hear's taken to court

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word in quotes is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: the word eye is said aloud, and it sounds just like the letter I
the 's is short for is, contributing its letter S
someone taken to court has been sued

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist printed gossip and was promptly sued for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'eye's sued' gives the answer: I, then the S of the 's (is), then SUED. 'Eye' might suggest Private Eye, the often-sued British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or magazine that has been put out to the public has been issued.

clue.text: Good dog! Fur finally more shiny

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of film and television

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: An owner praises a dog whose coat is glossier than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good dog!' reads as praise, but G and LASSIE are two pieces; LASSIE is the famous fictional collie.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass has a smooth gleaming surface, so a glassier finish is a glossier, more polished one.

clue.text: Sermon's appeal contains shock therapy

indicators.note: contains means the first piece is wrapped around the second

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or appeal
ECT stands for electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: A preacher's dramatic plea comes laced with electric treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Sermon' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture can be a moralising talk or telling-off, much like a preachy homily.

clue.text: Famous pop star 'posh' single in upset

indicators.note: in places the run of three pieces inside the word meaning upset

parts.note: to dish someone's plans is to upset or ruin them, past tense dished
Sting is the English rock singer, formerly of the Police
U stands for upper-class, an old label for posh language and manners
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: A celebrated singer, said to be posh, is unsettled about being unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' might suggest Posh Spice, but it gives U, the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eminent and widely respected, a notable figure, is called distinguished.

clue.text: Detective on dream branch

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
a vision is a dream or imagined sight

explanation.surface: A police officer pursues a hunch while working for a particular section.
explanation.definitionFit: A division is a section or department of a larger organisation, like an army or company.

clue.text: Digging beneath footing?

parts.note: beneath means under
one's footing or standing is one's position or status

explanation.surface: Someone excavates under the foundations of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digging' is the slang sense of 'dig', to grasp or appreciate something, not shovel work.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something in slang is to get it, so digging is comprehension.

clue.text: River craft with no go

indicators.note: with no means the following word's synonym is taken out

parts.note: industry can mean craft or diligent skilled work, and also trade
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A river boat lies idle, unable to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat on the river, but it is INDUSTRY in the sense of a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is the great river of Pakistan, flowing from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Chain letters not included by second post

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letter stands beside the rest
chain letters are the letters of chain jumbled up together with the following word

explanation.surface: A chain letter missed the post a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CHAIN with NOT included are rearranged to TANCHION, set beside S; 'included' just says NOT joins the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright bar or support, the same thing as a post.

clue.text: Iran tests the bomb — it's dropped for menaces

indicators.note: to bomb is to blow apart, so the letters of these words are scattered

parts.note: these three words are the pool of letters
these letters come out of the pool, said to be dropped

explanation.surface: Iran's weapon test alarms the world, which hears that the device has been released.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of IRAN TESTS THE, once I, T and S ('it's dropped') are taken out, rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten someone is to intimidate them, so both verbs mean warning of harm.

clue.text: Backing European union about metal combine

indicators.note: backing means the whole construction is read from right to left
about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A European bloc is reconsidering its policy on metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns round the whole assembly, not just 'European union'; 'about' is the container signal, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join or merge them into one.

clue.text: Commonly take the European line on metal

parts.note: to nick is informal British slang for to steal, take
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone casually adopts the official EU stance on metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks slang: NICK is informal British for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel is a silvery metallic element used in alloys and coins.

clue.text: Hot air blow by mouth

indicators.note: by puts the second piece next to the first

parts.note: a clap is a sharp blow, as in a clap on the back
trap is slang for the mouth, as in shut your trap

explanation.surface: Someone exhales warm breath through their lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense or empty talk, the same as windy bluster.

clue.text: Unrestrained desire embracing setter's answers

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece wraps around the second
unrestrained suggests letters let loose to roam into a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Wild longing grips the crossword compiler as they hunt for solutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answers' is plural noun: remedies are solutions to problems. The setter is ME, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies are cures or solutions to problems, so they are answers in that sense.

clue.text: A Brit injured in the German blast

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled piece within the German word

parts.note: die is a German word for the

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A British person is hurt in an explosion in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like an explosion, but it means an angry outburst; 'the German' is the German article DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast can be a furious verbal attack, a tirade or rant.

clue.text: Fearless united nations with a fine attack

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: The UN, undaunted, launches an assault with a penalty attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unafraid shows no fear, so they are brave or bold.

clue.text: Put on again for holiday season

parts.note: a holiday is a rest from work
an age or season is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone dresses again ready for the vacation period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' suggests getting dressed, but it means staging a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To restage a play is to mount a fresh production of it.

clue.text: Woman's support round butt!

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
a butt is the end of something, like a cigarette

explanation.surface: A lady's foundation garment encircles her rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Woman' reads as 'is'; 'butt' is not a backside but a stub end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a female given name.

clue.text: Party concerning party leader in party?

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: in puts the leading letter within the word for a faction

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party

indicators.note: leader means just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A political group debates its leader's role within the party.
explanation.walkthrough: RESPECT was a British left-wing political party founded in 2004, hence the question mark on 'Party' as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect was the name of a UK political movement, so the definition names it by example.

clue.text: Helicopter's top crew's altitude

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word, as this is a down clue

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A helicopter's senior crew member checks how high they are flying.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew; the 's after 'crew' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Height and altitude both describe distance above ground or sea level.

clue.text: Lots of models taking ecstasy

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes in the second

parts.note: an artist's model sits for a portrait, so models means sits
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Many fashion models are on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot is a plot of land, so lots are sites for building.

clue.text: Kept safe and secure in crush

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: to tread is to crush underfoot
sure means secure or firm

explanation.surface: Something was protected and safe in the middle of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasured things are cherished and carefully preserved, guarded closely.

clue.text: Dated contents of treasure trove

indicators.note: contents of means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Old items found within a hoard of buried riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates the past, so it looks old-fashioned.

clue.text: Gent with a man I suspect is coming out

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are untrustworthy and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentleman and another man are under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emanating is flowing or issuing from a source.

clue.text: Finished school, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be pronounced aloud

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone has left school, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English boarding school near Windsor; it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten is all gone, consumed.

clue.text: Election date endlessly changed for amusement

indicators.note: changed means the letters are put into a different order
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: Polling day was moved, to the public's great enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectation means delight or enjoyment.
